correctness.rationale: Rebuilt the invariant-plane disintegration: s=|u_z| is uniform before conditioning; hit interval length 2b h(s) makes p(s)=h/H and normalized signed offset v independent uniform [-1,1]. For Q=b^{-2}diag(1,1,r^{-2}), det(Q|u⊥)=h²/(b⁴r²), and slice reduction 1-v² gives X=r(1-v²)/h. Thus P(X>x)=H^{-1}∫h√(1-xh/r)_+ and E[X]=2r/(3H). Differentiating the survival (integrable endpoint) and substituting h=√(1+(r²-1)s²) yields exact density (1). At x=1 the upper endpoint weight W(r)=r²/[2H(r²-1)]; replacing y=r-h shows Δf=-2rW(r)√ε+O(ε) from below; moving-upper-limit sin² reparameterization from above gives analytic behavior; away from x=1 changes are analytic. Support [0,r], b=√(A_cusp/π), r=A_max/A_cusp. Independent SciPy quadratures at r=1.3,2,4,12 recovered left coefficients to within 0.0051 relative at ε=10^-5, with finite right slopes; independent 80,000-plane simulations for r=1.3,2,4 matched means and survival. Finite checks corroborate, not prove, exact asymptotics. Boundary ball r=1 explicitly excluded.

value.rationale: Natural Crofton invariant-plane sampling of a fixed spheroid induces a sharp, analytically nontrivial change in the range of allowed normal angles when raw area crosses the minor-axis disk area. The resulting universal fractional density coefficient and two-feature area-only reconstruction are structural and usable exact population invariants, distinct from classical section-ellipse size/shape inference. The 1986 numerical area histograms are credited, and no finite-observation/noise guarantee is asserted.

final_claim: For a fixed solid prolate spheroid with transverse semiaxis b>0 and aspect ratio r>1, a Euclidean-motion-invariant random affine plane conditioned to hit the spheroid gives normalized section area X=A/(πb²) with survival H^{-1}∫_0^1 h(s)√(1-xh(s)/r)_+ ds and continuous density analytic on (0,1) and (1,r), with unique interior one-sided square-root cusp at x=1: f_r(1-ε)=f_r(1)-r³/[H(r²-1)]√ε+O_r(ε), f_r(1+ε)=f_r(1)+O_r(ε). Its area cusp and upper support endpoint identify b and r; E[X]=2r/(3H).
limitations: A fixed prolate body and exact motion-invariant hitting-plane conditioning only; not a finite-sample inference guarantee or general ellipsoid/mixture result.
